decision: Sufficient official basis to implement a fail-closed transactional RunAtLogin candidate, followed by real scratch-registry interleaving tests; not proof of universal serializable compare-and-swap.

sources.fact: Subsequent operations on the opened key are transacted; non-transacted operations before commit cause rollback. Documentation does not specify every competing TxR read-set schedule, writer priority, blocking duration, or exact conflict error.
Handles bound to a transaction should be closed before commit. HKEY uses RegCloseKey; CloseHandle does not close registry keys.
FALSE reports failure with GetLastError; documentation does not establish that every failure proves no prior commit. Do not treat all failed/uncertain outcomes as mutation-free.
Outcome can be queried with TRANSACTION_QUERY_INFORMATION; inability to prove the outcome remains unknown.
A transaction must never be assumed active: it can be rolled back for many reasons and at any time.

candidate_sequence: Keep existing exact authority, intent, journal, and original deadline.
Begin one transaction; open existing fixed Run key transactionally; enabling a missing key requires a separately reviewed RegCreateKeyTransacted path.
Read bounded exact preimage and compare; fresh check before tentative transacted set/delete.
Treat staging as tentative, not as a committed mutation.
Actually RegCloseKey successfully before commit; perform final memory-only fresh check.
Commit, then classify actual outcome conservatively; rollback when applicable and check actual handle closure.
Only after transaction cleanup use ordinary observation; never fall back to ordinary set/delete.
scope_adjustment: The first report deliberately proposed negative-only deletion. Parent subsequently requested exploring both existing enable and disable paths; the documented handle-based mechanism supports that candidate direction without weakening original authority/journal policy.
limits: No claim of bounded native syscall completion or writer priority.
No claim all concurrent transactional read/write schedules are serializable.
No MSI account selection, full maintenance-owner lifecycle, runtime certification, or platform PASS is supplied by this research.
Cleanup failure must preserve exact owner and reject replacement, rather than report a logical cancellation as physical release.
verification_pending: Real scratch key external ordinary replacement between comparison and staging/commit.
Competing transactional writer timing and actual conflict outcomes.
Fresh-check cancellation, key absence, unsupported transaction manager, rollback/close failure and unknown outcome handling.
